title: Complete Pascal's Hexagon Theorem (Sylvester's Law sorry)

problemStatement.formal: \exists M : \text{Mat}_{3\times 3}(\mathbb{R}),\, \det M \neq 0 \land \forall p,\, p \in C \iff \pi(M)(p) \in C_0
problemStatement.plain: PascalsHexagon.lean (Wiedijk #77) has 1 sorry: Sylvester's law connecting an arbitrary real conic to the standard conic via a projective transformation. Prove using Mathlib's spectral theorem for quadratic forms.
whyMatters: Demonstrates projective equivalence of real conics
Classic application of Sylvester's law of inertia

proven: All Pascal constraint steps except Sylvester's law
open: Sylvester's law: any conic of signature (2,1) is congruent to x²+y²-z²
